sources.title: Multi-Bird Nutrition Research Findings
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Original Manus project research
sources.permittedUse: Protected evidence of original multi-bird research intent and original named source trail.
sources.limitations: Not a complete field-level citation ledger and cannot independently validate every ingredient or six-bird compatibility outcome.

sources.title: Preserved pigeon nutrition research and original ingredient catalog
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Original Manus project research
sources.permittedUse: Protected evidence of pigeon-only research, catalog lineage, target intent, and named reference list.
sources.limitations: Individual nutrient rows and formulation targets still need source-level locator mapping before live-data changes.

sources.title: Toxic Legumes for Pigeons - Research Findings
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Original Manus project research
sources.permittedUse: Protected record of original raw-legume safety and preparation intent.
sources.limitations: Its named research inputs include broad pet sources, rescue organizations, and forums; it requires stronger source-level validation before future runtime use.

sources.title: Nutritional Requirements
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Finch Information Center
sources.permittedUse: Canary/finch/passserine maintenance context, explicit limits on poultry extrapolation, and cited nutrient discussion.
sources.limitations: Approximate passerine allowances are not universal canary targets and cannot be copied to any other calculator species.

sources.title: Nutrition in Pigeons and Doves
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Joeke Nijboer, PhD; Anouk Fens, MSc; Merck Veterinary Manual
sources.permittedUse: Pigeon/dove feeding ecology, pellet context, and crop-milk/squab nutrition.
sources.limitations: Does not validate each dry-mix ingredient, racing profile, or all six species.

sources.title: Nutrition of the domestic pigeon (Columba livia domestica)
sources.authorsOrOrganization: J. Sales; G. P. J. Janssens
sources.permittedUse: Domestic pigeon nutrient, energy, whole-grain feeding, and species-difference review.
sources.limitations: Adult-production context does not automatically set pet, racing, breeding, or winter calculator targets without an explicit mapping decision.

sources.title: Nutrition in Psittacines
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Joeke Nijboer, PhD; Anouk Fens, MSc; Merck Veterinary Manual
sources.permittedUse: Psittacine feeding context, explicit Grey and budgerigar maintenance ranges, seed-diet limits, and grit distinction.
sources.limitations: A psittacine-general statement cannot be treated as a species-specific food approval for every parrot, Grey, or budgie record.

sources.title: Nutrition of Birds in the Order Psittaciformes: A Review
sources.authorsOrOrganization: E. A. Koutsos; K. D. Matson; K. C. Klasing
sources.permittedUse: Scientific framework for physiologically appropriate psittacine diet and related-species evidence assessment.
sources.limitations: Methodological review; it is not an ingredient-by-ingredient compatibility approval table.

sources.title: The diet of adult psittacids: veterinarian and ethological approaches
sources.authorsOrOrganization: F. Péron; C. Grosset
sources.permittedUse: Seed-mix limitations, selective feeding, captive-diet context, water-supplement risks, and cited Grey/budgie observations.
sources.limitations: Does not provide a six-bird food compatibility catalogue.

sources.title: African Grey Parrots - Feeding
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Gregory Rich, DVM; Laurie Hess, DVM, DABVP; Rick Axelson, DVM; VCA Animal Hospitals
sources.permittedUse: African Grey companion-care context for seed/nut moderation, calcium/vitamin-A risks, fresh food, water, and grit boundaries.
sources.limitations: Owner-facing veterinary guidance; not a complete nutrient or ingredient-analysis database.

sources.title: Nutritional Requirements of Poultry
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Doug Korver, PhD; Merck Veterinary Manual
sources.permittedUse: Chicken life-stage complete-ration, water, nutrient-density, amino-acid, vitamin, and mineral context.
sources.limitations: Does not make a dry seed, grain, or legume mix a complete chicken ration and cannot set requirements for other bird groups.

sources.title: Feeding Chickens for Egg Production in Small and Backyard Flocks
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Jacquie Jacob, DVM, PhD; University of Kentucky / Poultry Extension
sources.permittedUse: Chicken complete-feed, scratch-grain, grit, and life-stage feeding context for a diagnostic review of a scratch-supplement estimator.
sources.limitations: Backyard poultry guidance; it does not validate this application's individual ingredient nutrient values, optimization objective, profile targets, or a replacement chicken formula.

sources.title: Bulletin #2222, Nutrition for Backyard Chicken Flocks in Maine
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Donna R. Coffin; University of Maine Cooperative Extension
sources.permittedUse: Chicken life-stage complete-feed, controlled-grain, scratch-grain, protein, calcium, and grit context for a diagnostic review of a scratch-supplement estimator.
sources.limitations: Backyard and small-flock guidance; it is not a direct instruction to change an application's profile, formula, safety outcome, nutrient table, or visitor-visible wording.

sources.title: Nutrient Requirements of Poultry: Tenth Revised Edition
sources.authorsOrOrganization: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
sources.permittedUse: Current consensus backbone for poultry nutrient requirements, feed ingredients, bioavailability, and life-phase review.
sources.limitations: Future numeric rows must cite the exact edition, table, and life stage rather than the book title alone.

sources.title: Clinical Avian Medicine
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Greg J. Harrison, DVM; Teresa L. Lightfoot, DVM; contributing authors
sources.permittedUse: Cross-species chapter-level veterinary reference for nutrition, toxicology, racing pigeons, galliformes, and canaries/finches.
sources.limitations: Each future claim must cite its exact relevant chapter/section; the book title cannot act as blanket six-bird approval.

sources.title: Preserved pre-audit multi-bird profile configuration
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Original Manus project implementation
sources.permittedUse: Exact preservation of the pre-audit multi-bird profile configuration used for reconciliation.
sources.limitations: This configuration snapshot proves the previous implemented value; it is not a scientific source validating that value.

sources.title: Current V3 runtime profile configuration
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Bird Feed Calculator V3 implementation
sources.permittedUse: Exact snapshot of the currently configured V3 target ranges for reconciliation only.
sources.limitations: This is a live implementation snapshot, not a scientific source or a replacement for the protected original research.

sources.title: Ultraviolet Light as a Critical Component of Companion Bird Husbandry
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Donna Garrou; Harrison's Bird Foods
sources.permittedUse: General companion-bird UVB, vitamin-D, calcium-metabolism, window-glass, natural-sunlight, and artificial-lighting husbandry context.
sources.limitations: It does not prescribe a universal lamp, UV index, distance, or exposure duration for any calculator species; species-specific installation decisions require separately reviewed evidence.

sources.title: Effects of B-Wave Ultraviolet Supplementation Using Light-Emitting Diodes on Caged Laying Hens during the Later Phase of the Laying Cycle
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Yongxiang Wei; Weichao Zheng; Baoming Li; Qin Tong; Haipeng Shi; Xuanyang Li
sources.permittedUse: Direct laying-hen evidence on the studied UVB-LED intervention, vitamin-D physiology, calcium/phosphorus metabolism, and bone/laying outcomes.
sources.limitations: A controlled later-phase laying-hen study; it does not prescribe home fixture setup or extrapolate to pigeons, psittacines, or canaries.

sources.title: Feeding Pigeons and Doves
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Gregory Rich, DVM; Laurie Hess, DVM; Rick Axelson, DVM; VCA Animal Hospitals
sources.permittedUse: Pigeon/dove fresh-produce, fruit-portion, wash, size, separate-dish, daily-water, and shell-grit calcium context.
sources.limitations: It does not name apples as a pigeon-specific food and does not establish racing, breeding, or dry-formula inclusion rates.

sources.title: Diet for Pet Pigeons
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Melbourne Bird Veterinary Clinic
sources.permittedUse: Pet-pigeon diet context for vegetables, whole grain, small fruit portions, insects as enrichment, and fresh-produce examples.
sources.limitations: Explicitly excludes breeding and racing pigeon use and does not individually validate every fruit or vegetable for calculator inclusion.

sources.title: Canaries - Feeding
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Gregory Rich, DVM; Laurie Hess, DVM; Rick Axelson, DVM; VCA Animal Hospitals
sources.permittedUse: Canary fruit/vegetable preparation, portion, fresh-food, pelleted-diet, seed-diet, and apple-listing context.
sources.limitations: Owner-facing guidance, not an ingredient nutrient analysis or a direct basis for other passerines or other calculator species.

sources.title: Feeding Meyer's Parrots
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Gregory Rich, DVM; Laurie Hess, DVM; Rick Axelson, DVM; VCA Animal Hospitals
sources.permittedUse: Psittacine fresh-produce preparation, fruit moderation, and explicit apple-seed avoidance context.
sources.limitations: Meyer's-parrot guidance is group-level support only; it cannot silently approve every parrot species or set African Grey and budgie portions.

sources.title: Budgies – Feeding
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Gregory Rich, DVM; Laurie Hess, DVM; Rick Axelson, DVM; VCA Animal Hospitals
sources.permittedUse: Budgie fresh-produce preparation, fruit/vegetable diet boundary, and explicit apple-listing context.
sources.limitations: Owner-facing budgie guidance; it does not establish nutritional values or validate food use for any other species.

sources.title: Fruits and Vegetables in Birds' Diets
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Gregory Rich, DVM; Laurie Hess, DVM; Rick Axelson, DVM; VCA Animal Hospitals
sources.permittedUse: Broad companion-bird apple listing, produce washing, size, variety, and base-diet context.
sources.limitations: Broad guidance does not replace a named species' review and cannot turn an unresolved species row into approval by itself.

sources.title: Nutritional Diseases of Pet Birds
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Sharman M. Hoppes, DVM, Dipl ABVP (Avian); Merck Veterinary Manual
sources.permittedUse: Broad pet-bird safety exclusion for apple seeds and nutrition-disease context.
sources.limitations: The listed apple-seed exclusion does not independently establish apple-flesh suitability or a portion for every species.

sources.title: 10 Foods You Should Never Feed Chickens
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Kalyn Waters; UF/IFAS Extension
sources.permittedUse: Chicken-specific statement that apple fruit is safe when seeds are removed, plus apple-seed/pit avoidance.
sources.limitations: Extension owner guidance; it does not provide an apple feeding dose or replace a balanced chicken ration.

sources.title: Backyard & Small Poultry Flock Management Series: Feeding the Laying Hen
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Wilmer Pacheco; Joseph Gulizia; Kevin Downs; Alabama Extension
sources.permittedUse: Complete-feed foundation, sparing-treatment boundary, calcium/eggshell context, and chicken feeding-management evidence.
sources.limitations: It does not identify apples as a required ration component or set a fruit portion; treats remain incomplete feeds.

sources.title: Fruits and vegetables
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Modern Pet Pigeon Society Wiki
sources.permittedUse: Pigeon-specific companion-care guidance that explicitly lists fresh apple flesh among produce options and sets wash, small-piece, fruit-treat, and apple-seed-exclusion boundaries.
sources.limitations: Community-maintained owner guidance. Its cited references support context but it is not a nutrient analysis, a complete-ration rule, or evidence for dry-mix inclusion rates.

sources.title: What do pigeons eat | Complete Guide
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Ismail Hossain; Pigeon Care Tips
sources.permittedUse: Corroborative pigeon-specific keeper guidance that names small apple pieces as an occasional fresh-food addition alongside a grain-and-seed main diet.
sources.limitations: Non-veterinary online guidance with no cited evidence trail on the page. It is corroborative only and cannot establish nutrient values, medicinal claims, formula inclusion, or portions.

sources.title: Pigeon feeding & dove feeding
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Palomacy Pigeon & Dove Adoptions
sources.permittedUse: Pigeon/dove rescue guidance for washed, finely chopped vegetables and greens as separate fresh-food additions with clean water and pigeon-safe grit context.
sources.limitations: Rescue/owner guidance that does not name apple or establish a full fresh-produce nutrient plan, dry-mix inclusion rate, or universal feeding schedule.

sources.title: Soaks and Sprouts: A Nutritional Powerhouse for Parrots
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Michelle “Elle” Magnon; The Happy Cockatoo: Elle's Avian Cuisine
sources.permittedUse: Direct parrot-specific owner guidance that names garbanzo beans/chickpeas and states that legumes are not safe raw; it requires sprouting to visible root tails before feeding.
sources.limitations: Experienced parrot keeper guidance, not peer-reviewed or clinical guidance. It does not establish a cooking method, portion, nutrition value, complete ration, runtime food approval, or outcome for pigeons, African Greys, budgies, canaries, or chickens.

sources.title: Including Chickpeas in Organic Poultry Diets
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Jacquie Jacob, PhD; University of Kentucky / eOrganic
sources.permittedUse: Chicken/poultry context for chickpea antinutritional factors, raw-chickpea inclusion research, heat-treatment considerations, and complete-ration limitations.
sources.limitations: Extension guidance summarizing feed studies; it does not establish a household feeding method, a complete ration, or suitability for pigeons, psittacines, budgies, or canaries.

sources.title: Raw Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) as a Substitute of Soybean Meal in Compound Feed for Broiler Chickens
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Anna Danek-Majewska; Małgorzata Kwiecień; Anna Winiarska-Mieczan; Małgorzata Haliniarz; Agata Bielak
sources.permittedUse: Controlled broiler-chicken evidence for raw chickpea seed used within specified formulated grower and finisher diets.
sources.limitations: A Ross 308 broiler production study; it does not establish unsupervised household feeding, a complete ration, a universal inclusion level, or suitability for any other supported bird.

sources.title: What can budgies eat?
sources.authorsOrOrganization: ExoticDirect
sources.permittedUse: Budgie-specific owner guidance that explicitly lists chickpeas among foods that should not be fed raw.
sources.limitations: Commercial insurer guidance without named clinical authors or an evidence list. It is limited to a raw-form preparation boundary and does not establish a cooking method, nutrition value, portion, complete ration, or another species outcome.

sources.title: Parakeet Food List
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Omlet
sources.permittedUse: Budgie/parakeet food-form guidance that explicitly lists whole, threshed wheat among parakeet-friendly grains and distinguishes fresh hulled grain from cooked or processed forms.
sources.limitations: Owner guidance rather than a peer-reviewed feeding trial; it cannot approve wheat for parrots, African Greys, canaries, pigeons, or chickens and does not establish a complete ration.

sources.title: Wheat in Poultry Diets
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Jacquie Jacob, PhD; University of Kentucky Poultry Extension
sources.permittedUse: Chicken/poultry feed context for wheat varieties, whole-wheat inclusion, nutrient composition, and processing/mold-management boundaries.
sources.limitations: Poultry feed guidance does not make wheat a complete ration, does not establish companion-bird suitability, and does not remove the need to formulate for life stage and nutrient balance.

sources.title: The Nutrition of the Racing Pigeons
sources.authorsOrOrganization: J. Aubrey Mire; Pigeon Vitality
sources.permittedUse: Racing-pigeon grain-ration context naming corn, sorghum, wheat, peas, and their nutrient roles.
sources.limitations: Racing context and owner guidance; it cannot set companion-pigeon portions, approve other species, or replace a complete veterinary review.

sources.title: What can budgies eat?
sources.authorsOrOrganization: ExoticDirect
sources.permittedUse: Budgie-specific food lists and preparation cautions for grains, millet, peas, and legumes.
sources.limitations: Owner guidance rather than a controlled feeding study; it cannot approve these forms for other species or establish a complete ration.

sources.title: Feeding Value of Lupins, Field Peas, Faba Beans and Chickpeas for Poultry: An Overview
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Laura S. David; Catootjie L. Nalle; M. Reza Abdollahi; Velmurugu Ravindran
sources.permittedUse: Poultry feeding value, antinutritional factors, and processing context for field peas and chickpeas.
sources.limitations: Poultry review; it does not establish companion-bird suitability, raw-food safety for the six supported birds, or a complete ration by itself.

sources.title: Canary diet
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Lafeber Pet Birds
sources.permittedUse: Canary-specific guidance for occasional dried-mealworm treats, including molt and breeding-conditioning context and sparing-use limits.
sources.limitations: A veterinary owner-answer rather than a controlled feeding trial; it does not establish live mealworm, cricket, pigeon, parrot, African Grey, budgie, or chicken outcomes.

sources.title: Insects as Feed for Companion and Exotic Pets: A Current Trend
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Fabrizzio Valdés; Valeria Villanueva; Emerson Durán; Francisca Campos; Constanza Avendaño; Manuel Sánchez; Chaneta Domingoz-Araujo; Carolina Valenzuela
sources.permittedUse: Broad exotic-pet context for mealworms and house crickets in whole, live, or dehydrated formats, with evidence-scarcity and safety limitations.
sources.limitations: The review says species-specific safety and feeding evidence for exotic pets is limited; it cannot silently approve any named calculator bird or portion.

sources.title: Insect meal as a feed ingredient for poultry
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Usman Elahi; Chang-chun Xu; Jing Wang; Jing Lin; Shu-geng Wu; Hai-jun Zhang; Guang-hai Qi
sources.permittedUse: Poultry feed context for mealworm, cricket, earthworm, and other insect meals; distinguishes live, dried, and paste forms and discusses hygiene and disease-carrier risks.
sources.limitations: Poultry review; it does not establish companion-bird suitability, household treat portions, or a complete ration from insects alone.

sources.title: Black soldier fly and yellow mealworm live larvae for broiler chickens: Effects on bird performance and health status
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Sara Bellezza Oddon; Ilaria Biasato; Arianna Imarisio; Miha Pipan; Dominik Dekleva; Elena Colombino; Maria Teresa Capucchio; Marco Meneguz; Stefania Bergagna; Raffaella Barbero; Marta Gariglio; Sihem Dabbou; Edoardo Fiorilla; Laura Gasco; Achille Schiavone
sources.permittedUse: Controlled broiler study of limited live yellow mealworm larvae as environmental enrichment alongside a commercial diet.
sources.limitations: Broiler strain, age, quantity, and study conditions are specific; it cannot establish pet-bird outcomes or a general mealworm feeding amount.

sources.title: Pigeon Diet Guide
sources.authorsOrOrganization: CPC Staff; Columbidae Ownership Omnibus
sources.permittedUse: Pigeon-specific owner guidance naming dried lentils, split peas, mung beans, and dried peas as feed-mix or treat context.
sources.limitations: Community guidance with an empty references section. It does not establish raw-legume safety, preparation, portion, nutrient values, formula inclusion, or kidney-bean use; it supports only the exact named pigeon ingredient context.

sources.title: Cooking Beans for Parrots
sources.authorsOrOrganization: David Poole; Petcraft
sources.permittedUse: Parrot-focused preparation context explicitly naming lentils and yellow/green split peas as pulses to cook before offering.
sources.limitations: Owner guidance, not a controlled feeding study. It does not establish a species-specific dose, a universal cooking protocol, a complete ration, runtime approval, or an outcome for pigeons, African Greys, budgies, canaries, or chickens.

sources.title: Legume Safety Warning
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Shauna Roberts; For the Birds Parrot Rescue & Sanctuary
sources.permittedUse: Parrot-rescue preparation guidance that identifies lentils, mung beans, and sweet/green peas as sproutable and says kidney beans should be fully cooked.
sources.limitations: Rescue owner guidance, not a controlled feeding trial. It does not establish a preparation method, portion, complete ration, runtime approval, or outcome for pigeons, African Greys, budgies, canaries, or chickens.

sources.title: Beneficial Effects of Increasing Dietary Levels of Raw Lentil Seeds on Meat Fatty Acid and Plasma Metabolic Profile in Broiler Chickens
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Georgeta Ciurescu; Andreea Vasilachi; Mariana Ropotă; Mihai Palade; Cătălin Dragomir
sources.permittedUse: Controlled Cobb 500 broiler evidence for raw lentil seed within specified balanced experimental diets at stated inclusion levels.
sources.limitations: Broiler production study only; it does not establish household feeding, a universal inclusion rate, a complete ration, or an outcome for pigeons, psittacines, budgies, canaries, or another legume form.

sources.title: Performance and Histological Responses of Internal Organs of Broiler Chickens Fed Raw, Dehulled, and Aqueous and Dry-Heated Kidney Bean Meals
sources.authorsOrOrganization: I. A. Emiola; A. D. Ologhobo; R. M. Gous
sources.permittedUse: Controlled 56-day broiler evidence comparing raw and processed kidney-bean meals within stated experimental diets and documenting the reported performance and organ-histology boundary.
sources.limitations: Broiler production study only; it does not prescribe a household preparation method, a complete ration, or an outcome for pigeons, psittacines, budgies, canaries, or another legume form.
